subject: Post-call: Ops visibility & hyperscaler comparison — agreed next tests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Varga <sara.varga@acme-logistics.com>, platform@acme-logistics.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Ops visibility & hyperscaler comparison — agreed next tests

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an actionable plan. Appreciate you and Tom walking through the platform constraints and telemetry goals.

Recap (high level)
- Acme goals: 1) 99th percentile tail latency under 350ms for 512-token responses; 2) consistent traceability from request-id -> token stream; 3) cost bucket visibility (tokens per feature, per-route).
- Competitive context: youre evaluating Redwood vs Hyperscaler A hosted endpoint and Hyperscaler B managed inference. We discussed differences in streaming latency, per-token unit cost, and tracing integration.

Agreed tests (what we propose to run next week)
- Latency + streaming tail test (p50/p95/p99) against same prompt set across: Redwood hosted, Hyperscaler A endpoint, Hyperscaler B managed model.
- Trace fidelity check: emit request-id + span for each chunk; validate correlate across Prometheus + tracing backend (Jaeger/OTEL).
- Cost & sample billing reconciliation: produce 1M token run and show per-route token accounting; check token-metering parity.
- Dashboard ingestion test: push our sample telemetry to your Grafana datasource and confirm chart parity (token count, cost estimate, live stream latency).

Attachments: call recording + gap matrix + proposed test plan attached for your review.

Immediate asks for Acme
- Can you drop the telemetry spec you referenced (schema + retention) and confirm access to the Grafana instance or provide a read-only data source?
- Confirm which Hyperscaler endpoints we should include (endpoint URLs or account names).

Proposed timing
- Start tests: Tue Jun 9 (AM PT) — Redwood engineering runs parallel tests; we plan to share a live dashboard link by EOD Tue and a short write-up Wed morning.

Thanks — Ill own scheduling. Laura will own the Grafana integration, Jordan will own test harness and data collection.

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: call-recording-20260608.mp4 (audio), ops-visibility-gap-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-plan.md (doc)

From: Sara Varga <sara.varga@acme-logistics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Huang <tom.huang@acme-logistics.com>, platform@acme-logistics.com, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Ops visibility & hyperscaler comparison — agreed next tests

Thanks Ben — clear summary, appreciate the structure. Quick answers:
- Telemetry spec: attached the "acme-internal-telemetry-spec.pdf" (schema + example traces). Please confirm you can emit the fields we listed: request_id, route, model_variant, token_index, chunk_latency_ms.
- Hyperscaler endpoints: include these two test slots: hyperscaler-a-prod-infer.acme (contact: tom.huang@acme-logistics.com) and hyperscaler-b-managed.acme.
- Grafana: we can provision a read-only API key for a dedicated test dashboard. Ill have platform@acme-logistics.com send the key by Tue AM.

Priority: please focus on p99 tail and streaming chunk latency first; billing parity can be secondary for this run but still needed by next Wed.

Two asks from our side: 1) can you share a short specification for how Redwood reports token usage (fields, timestamps)? 2) wed like a short deck comparing Redwood streaming latency approach vs Hyperscaler A (single-slide, 1 page) for the executive review.

Ill schedule a 30m sync Wed 10:00 AM PT to check progress.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Varga
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Logistics
sara.varga@acme-logistics.com

Attachment: acme-internal-telemetry-spec.pdf (schema)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Ops visibility & hyperscaler comparison — agreed next tests

Ben / Laura — quick internal note after reading Saras spec (excerpted below).

> Please confirm you can emit the fields we listed: request_id, route, model_variant, token_index, chunk_latency_ms.

We can emit all of those today. Proposed owners and timeline:
- Test harness (parallel runners + prompt set): Jordan (me) — 1 day to configure, runs Tue AM and Tue PM to check variance.
- Trace export to their Jaeger: Laura — integrate OTLP exporter to push sampled spans; validate correlation on Tuesday afternoon.
- Dashboard integration: Laura to create Grafana dashboard using Acme read-only key (plots: p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming chunk latency distribution, token-per-route counts) — target Wed morning.
- Billing token reconciliation: Jordan + Ben — generate canonical 1M token run and compare our meter vs Hyperscaler metrics; target Wed EOD.

Metrics to capture (minimal set)
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (ms)
- per-chunk latency histogram (streaming)
- tokens consumed per request and per-route token totals
- error/retry rate and tail impact on latency

Risks / notes
- Hyperscaler A enforces a different chunking behavior; we should normalize by token boundaries, not chunk boundaries. I will add a small normalization step in the harness.
- Sampling rates: confirm whether Acmes Jaeger endpoint requires OTLP with batching or accepts single-span push. Laura will test both.

Ill push the initial run logs to the Drive folder and flag any anomalies in Slack.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Varga <sara.varga@acme-logistics.com>, Tom Huang <tom.huang@acme-logistics.com>, platform@acme-logistics.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Ops visibility & hyperscaler comparison — agreed next tests

Sara / Tom — thanks for the quick turn. Short update and calendar invites attached.

What were delivering by Wed EOD (and handoff)
- Live dashboard link with p50/p95/p99 latency and streaming chunk histograms (Laura).
- Test harness results: raw logs + normalized latency table for Redwood, Hyperscaler A, Hyperscaler B (Jordan).
- 1-page executive slide: streaming latency approach comparison + cost delta summary (Ben).
- Billing reconciliation dataset for 1M token run (CSV) and notes on how our meter maps to Hyperscaler counters.

Next coordination steps
- Laura: please confirm Grafana read-only key arrival and post the dashboard link in the Drive folder.
- Jordan: start the harness Tue AM and run the normalization. Post initial results to Drive under /ops-poc/runs/2026-06-09.
- Sara / Platform: send the Grafana key + Hyperscaler endpoint details.

Links & artifacts
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/57821
- Shared drive (tests + dashboards): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/xyz-observability-poc
- Initial test plan (internal): https://redwood-internal/reports/benchmark-2026-05

If we hit the latency targets on Redwood and show parity in trace fidelity, next step is a short POC to run a subset of production traffic for two weeks (low risk). Well capture SLIs and a rollback plan.

Thanks — Ill join the Wed 10:00 AM PT sync.

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: call-recording-20260608.mp4, ops-visibility-gap-matrix.xlsx, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-plan.md
